provenance: Entirely invented for illustration. No real organisation, person, product or measurement appears here. Replace it with your own questions before trusting any number it produces.
notes: Every question names the document that should be cited. must_abstain cases have no correct source: the system passes by declining to cite anything, and fails by citing something.

documents.title: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe — roast profile v3
documents.text: Charge temperature 196C. First crack observed at 8:42 with bean temperature 201C. Development time ratio 21%. Total roast 11:05, drop temperature 210C. Airflow raised to setting 4 at 7:30. Batch size 1.2 kg green.

documents.title: Colombia Huila — roast profile v3
documents.text: Charge temperature 202C. First crack at 9:10, bean temperature 203C. Development time ratio 24%. Total roast 12:00, drop temperature 213C. Batch size 1.2 kg green. Airflow held at setting 3 throughout.

documents.title: Cupping session 2031-03-04
documents.text: Panel of five. Ethiopia Yirgacheffe v3 scored 86.5 overall; notes of bergamot and stone fruit, acidity bright. Colombia Huila v3 scored 84.0; heavier body, cocoa finish, acidity muted. Two panellists flagged the Huila as slightly baked.

documents.title: Roaster maintenance log — Q1
documents.text: 2031-01-12 replaced chaff collector gasket. 2031-02-03 recalibrated bean probe; offset was reading 4C low before adjustment. 2031-03-01 drum bearing inspected, no play detected. Next probe calibration due 2031-08-03.

documents.title: Green inventory and moisture
documents.text: Ethiopia Yirgacheffe lot 7734: 42 kg remaining, moisture 10.8%, water activity 0.55. Colombia Huila lot 8120: 61 kg remaining, moisture 11.4%, water activity 0.58. Both stored at 18C, 55% RH.

questions.question: What was the drop temperature on the Ethiopia Yirgacheffe v3 roast?
questions.rationale: 210C, stated directly in the roast profile.

questions.question: Which coffee scored higher at the March cupping, and by how much?
questions.rationale: Ethiopia 86.5 vs Colombia 84.0 — a 2.5 point difference, both in one document.

questions.question: Compare the development time ratios of the two v3 profiles.
questions.rationale: 21% vs 24% — requires both profiles, so it tests that the per-source cap still admits two documents.

questions.question: When is the next bean probe calibration due?
What is the water activity of the Colombia Huila green lot?
questions.rationale: 0.58. Near-duplicate wording to the Ethiopia entry, so it tests that the right row is read.

questions.question: In the roast-profiles notebook, what airflow setting was used for the Ethiopia?
questions.rationale: Names its container, so it exercises scope detection.

questions.question: What was the charge temperature for the Colombia Huila?
questions.rationale: 202C. The Ethiopia profile states 196C for the same field — a conflation trap.

questions.question: How much Ethiopia Yirgacheffe green is left in stock?
What did the panel say about the Huila's body?
questions.rationale: Heavier body, cocoa finish — prose rather than a number.

questions.question: What was the probe offset error before the February recalibration?
What was the drop temperature on the Kenya Nyeri roast?
questions.rationale: No Kenya document exists. The failure mode is answering with the Ethiopia or Colombia value.

questions.question: What is our target moisture specification for incoming green coffee?
questions.rationale: Measured moisture values exist; a target specification does not. Tests measurement-vs-specification confusion.

questions.question: Who roasted the Ethiopia batch on 2031-03-04?
How long after first crack was the Ethiopia dropped?
questions.rationale: 11:05 minus 8:42 = 2:23. Requires arithmetic over cited values, not a lookup.

questions.question: Both v3 profiles used the same batch size — what was it?
questions.rationale: 1.2 kg green in both. Either document alone justifies the value; citing both is ideal.
